answer: We define a mechanism utilizing quartz hardware collateral within dynamic opportunity-cost bonds to anchor network presence. This relic of classical staking evolves into a subgame-perfect punishment matrix wherein identity multiplication triggers slashing penalties exceeding all marginal utility gains. By synchronizing state transitions to a cryptographic pulse derived from zero-knowledge verifiable delay functions, we prove that expected adversarial payoffs are strictly negative, forcing a unique Nash equilibrium favored by honest participation.
